test.name: GPS review of an existing proof routes to the gps-mentor agent, not this skill
test.description: Reviewing an EXISTING proof is the gps-mentor agent's job, not this skill's. Per the ruling on issue #1861 proof-conclusion's description no longer claims the review utterances and gps-mentor's claims them directly, so this test pins that the request does NOT land here. The mid-research-flynn scenario already has ps_001 (parentage, probable), and proof-conclusion's body has no review step: it resolves the request to one q_ id and delegates to the proof-conclusion agent to CONCLUDE, which would re-run the very conclusion the user asked to have judged. Graded on a routing-independent invariant rather than on a clean decline, because the model reliably answers a review request in-body instead of declining — the structurally unwinnable shape citation refuse-new-source, conflict-resolution negative-assertion-classification and tree-edit ut_003 all resolved with grade_on_invariant. Was a positive review-mode test before #1861; the user_message is unchanged so the utterance stays pinned in the trigger corpus.

input.user_message: Does my proof for the parentage question (ps_001) meet the Genealogical Proof Standard? Assess the EXISTING ps_001 against the five GPS components — judge it on the evidence it actually cites. Any sources or assertions that exist in research.json but are NOT cited in ps_001 are evidence GAPS for the next round of work (after they're extracted/classified) — flag them and say whether they would change the tier, but do NOT frame them as defects, failures, or premature reasoning of the current proof. Treat ps_001 as it stands.

negative.explanation: Routing is deliberately NOT graded here, and `correct_skill` is inert because `grade_on_invariant` makes _compute_outcome return before it reads routing. Measured 2026-09-01: the same utterance reached the `research` orchestrator on ut_proof_conclusion_007 and no skill at all on ut_proof_conclusion_r7k. Neither array value is correct for the pair — `[]` fails the run that routed to the orchestrator, and `["research"]` fails the run that routed nowhere — so the outcome is decided by the deterministic invariant instead: proof-conclusion must not activate, must write no new proof_summaries, and must leave ps_001.narrative_markdown byte-identical. Enforced by the three `gps-review`-tagged validators in eval/harness/validators/test_proof_conclusion.py. This is the shape citation refuse-new-source and tree-edit ut_003 already resolved the same way. The `evaluations` write both runs performed is a separate defect and is filed on its own; its absence from the invariant is not approval of it.

judge_context: Correct behavior is to route this to the gps-mentor agent — either by delegating to it, or by naming it as the right reviewer. Do NOT penalize a run that delegates to gps-mentor and relays its verdict.

proof-conclusion must NOT activate. Re-running the conclusion, writing or updating a proof_summaries entry for q_001, or writing to tree.gedcomx.json are all failures — the user asked for an assessment of ps_001 as it stands, not a rewrite.
Fail Correctness if the run produces a new or updated proof_summaries entry, or resolves q_001.

A reply that assesses ps_001 against the five GPS components WITHOUT invoking proof-conclusion is not a failure of this test — the routing gate is what this test measures, and the assessment's craft quality is the mentor's concern, not this skill's.
